# Volume 2 — XXII Odds and Ends

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

“Did you have tea with Rosalind Penrose at the stone house?” Thirza inquired while sitting at the breakfast table the following morning. “How does she appear these days? More than fifteen years have elapsed since our last meeting . . . that occurred on a Sunday inside Welby church. I imagine she is quite different now. Robin Farrow, whenever an item is out of your reach, request someone to hand it to you instead of stretching across the table like that. Did Cedric Stanhope ever behave in such a manner when he ate his meals with us?”
{: #nw-v02-c22-p0000 }

“However, Cedric’s arms possess greater length than mine,” grumbled Robin. “They have enjoyed eleven years of growth, whereas mine have merely had seven. Furthermore, I actually did make a request, but you and Nell were engaged in such deep conversation that you failed to pay any attention. Furthermore, Cedric has not ever been present here for any meal save for tea, and exercising politeness is simpler during tea than during breakfast. Your hunger is not nearly as great. An immense amount of time passes between supper and breakfast. At present, Nell, that spoonful is not a bit larger than it was a year ago, yet my size is significantly greater.”
{: #nw-v02-c22-p0001 }

“Naturally, I am unaware of how Miss Rosalind appeared in the past, yet I somehow doubt she has altered very much,” Nell remarked, following her assistance in serving Robin maple syrup, handing him two spoonfuls to quiet him down. “Her hair may be as white as snow, but her complexion remains bright and nearly like a young girl's, featuring the most delightful brown eyes . . . a lovely tone of wood-brown filled with tiny flecks of gold . . . while her voice recalls white satin, splashing water, and fairy bells all blended together.”
{: #nw-v02-c22-p0002 }

“In her youth, people considered her a major beauty,” Thirza remarked. “Although I was not acquainted with her intimately, she pleased me to the extent that I was familiar with her. Even in those days, certain individuals viewed her as odd. Robin, if I ever discover you engaging in that sort of prank another time, you will be forced to delay your dining until all the others have finished, in the manner of the French.”
{: #nw-v02-c22-p0003 }

The majority of talks that occurred between Nell and Thirza while in the company of the twins were broken up by these admonitions directed at Robin. On this occasion, Robin, it grieves one to say, failed to scrape together the final drops of his syrup using his spoon, so he resolved the problem by raising his plate with his two hands and licking it with his tiny pink tongue. Nell stared at him using eyes so filled with horror that the young offender blushed and uttered, partly embarrassed, partly boldly,
{: #nw-v02-c22-p0004 }

“No part is ruined when done like that.”
{: #nw-v02-c22-p0005 }

“Individuals who diverge from the norm are consistently labeled peculiar,” Nell remarked. “Miss Rosalind is undoubtedly distinct, even if pinpointing the exact nature of that dissimilarity proves difficult. Her status as a person who never ages might account for it.”
{: #nw-v02-c22-p0006 }

“A person may just as well age along with the rest of their peers,” remarked Thirza, paying little heed to her grammatical choices. “Failing to do so leaves you without a place anywhere. From what I am able to gather, Rosalind Penrose has simply withdrawn from all social life. By residing in that isolated spot, she has caused everyone to forget her existence. That dwelling made of stone stands as one of the Island’s most ancient structures. Eight decades in the past, after arriving from England, old Mr. Penrose constructed it. Robin, quit bumping Lucy’s arm. Oh, my eyes were on you! There is no point in attempting to appear blameless. Whatever is causing your misconduct like this today?”
{: #nw-v02-c22-p0007 }

“Perhaps I rose from the incorrect side of my bed,” Robin proposed. “Milty Gammon claims that doing so ensures your whole day will turn out badly. That came from his grandmother. But how do you tell which side is correct? Also, how can you manage if the wall is right up against your bed? I am looking for answers.”
{: #nw-v02-c22-p0008 }

“I’ve always pondered what occurred to ruin things between Stephen Stanhope and Rosalind Penrose,” Thirza went on, paying no attention to Robin. “They were undeniably betrothed twenty-five years back, and then, without warning, it ended. I am unaware of what the issue was, yet it had to be a dreadful thing, because he departed for the States and has not returned home ever since.”
{: #nw-v02-c22-p0009 }

“It might not have been anything so terrible, when all is said. In my view, minor occurrences in existence frequently cause greater difficulty than major ones,” Nell remarked, displaying a moment of understanding that no amount of living could have improved upon. “Thirza, I beg you not to mention to Mrs. Sowerby that I was at Miss Rosalind’s. She would certainly pose endless inquiries, and somehow I would prefer it not to happen . . . and I am certain Miss Rosalind would not care for it either, were she aware.”
{: #nw-v02-c22-p0010 }

“I suppose Agatha might be interested,” Thirza conceded, “even if she lacks the leisure she once enjoyed to attend to the business of others. Thomas’s condition keeps her bound to the house these days; moreover, her spirits are quite low, as I believe she is starting to give up on his recovery. Should he pass away, Agatha will find herself rather isolated, considering that every one of her offspring has relocated out west, barring Eliza who resides in town; and she holds no affection for her son-in-law.”
{: #nw-v02-c22-p0011 }

Thirza’s choice of words brought dishonor upon Eliza, whose devotion to her spouse was deep.
{: #nw-v02-c22-p0012 }

“Agatha claims he would recover if he would merely pull himself together and use his willpower. However, why ask a jellyfish to sit upright?” Thirza went on. “Thomas Sowerby has never possessed any willpower to use. His mother commanded him until his marriage, and Agatha took over after that. It is surprising he ventured to fall ill without obtaining her approval. Still, I ought not to speak in this manner. Agatha has proven to be a devoted wife to him. Without her, he surely would have come to nothing. He was created to be commanded; and fortunately, he ended up in the care of a smart, competent director like Agatha. Her methods did not bother him. They spared him the trouble of ever deciding anything for himself. Robin, please cease wriggling like an eel.”
{: #nw-v02-c22-p0013 }

“There is nothing else for me to do,” Robin objected. “I am unable to eat another bite, and seeing you and Nell eating is not enjoyable.”
{: #nw-v02-c22-p0014 }

“Well, you and Lucy step outside and feed the wheat to the hens,” Thirza said. “And also do not attempt to yank any further feathers from the white rooster’s tail.”
{: #nw-v02-c22-p0015 }

“I wished for a few feathers to make an Injun headpiece,” Robin uttered sullenly. “Milty Gammon possesses a fine one, fashioned from the feathers his mother provided to him after she slaughtered their elderly white gobbler. You could allow me to take a few. That rooster possesses far more than he requires.”
{: #nw-v02-c22-p0016 }

“The old feather duster in the garret is yours,” said Nell, “and for you, I’ll dye them yellow and red and green.”
{: #nw-v02-c22-p0017 }

“That boy is spoiled dreadfully by you,” Thirza remarked, after Robin, his countenance glowing, had gone out behind proper Lucy. Over the previous six years, Thirza had made immense progress in her education; nevertheless, she still could not free herself from the belief that gratifying a child’s desires too frequently was extremely harmful to it.
{: #nw-v02-c22-p0018 }

“Robin wishes for an Indian headdress because every other boy in his class possesses one,” Nell stated. “I understand that emotion . . . my desire for puffed sleeves back when every other girl wore them is something I will always remember. Furthermore, Robin is not being ruined. His behavior gets better with each passing day. Consider how much he has changed from the time he arrived here one year ago.”
{: #nw-v02-c22-p0019 }

“Since he started attending school, his involvement in trouble has definitely decreased,” Thirza conceded. “I imagine he exhausts that inclination alongside his peers. Still, I find it surprising that Richard Farrow hasn't contacted us prior to now. There hasn't been a single message since previous May.”
{: #nw-v02-c22-p0020 }

“I’ll be terrified to get news from him,” sighed Nell, starting to pack up the dishes. “In the event that a letter arrives, I’d be frightened to open it, because it might instruct us to ship the twins to his place.”
{: #nw-v02-c22-p0021 }

One month afterward, a missive arrived indeed. However, it had not been sent by Richard Farrow. An acquaintance of his had written to inform us that Richard Farrow had passed away from consumption two weeks prior. The author of the missive served as the executor of his testament, and through that testament, the amount of two thousand dollars was bequeathed to Miss Thirza Abernethy held in trust for David and Lucy Farrow until their adulthood or marriage. During the intervening period, the generated interest was to be applied toward their care.
{: #nw-v02-c22-p0022 }

“It feels terrible to feel happy about anything related to someone dying,” Nell remarked thoughtfully. “My heart goes out to poor Mr. Farrow; however, I am pleased that the twins can remain with us.”
{: #nw-v02-c22-p0023 }

“The money is a very fortunate matter,” Thirza remarked pragmatically. “My desire was to retain them, yet I truly failed to perceive how I might manage the expense, particularly as they advanced in age. What the farm yields in rent merely maintains the residence, and I was resolved that not a single penny of your funds would be expended upon them. Indeed, your contributions to them are already excessive. That new hat you purchased for Lucy was as unnecessary to her as two tails would be to a cat. However, the path has now opened up, and their future is secured.”
{: #nw-v02-c22-p0024 }

Robin and Lucy felt immense joy upon learning that Grey Shutters would be their home "for good." The passing of an uncle they had never met was completely insignificant to them when weighed against such news. Nevertheless, a single doubt troubled Lucy.
{: #nw-v02-c22-p0025 }

“Did they bury Uncle Richard?” she asked Nell in a whisper.
{: #nw-v02-c22-p0026 }

“Certainly, my love, naturally.”
{: #nw-v02-c22-p0027 }

“Is he . . . is he . . . anything like Mirabel Cotton’s uncle?” she asked in a whisper that was even more troubled. “He won’t roam around homes once he’s been put in the ground, will he, Nell?”
{: #nw-v02-c22-p0028 }
